blocks.title: Storing your file
blocks.body:
We will keep your file for {{retention}} after the matter ends. After that it may be destroyed securely without further notice unless you ask us in writing to keep it longer.
The file includes our correspondence, notes and copies of documents. Original documents are returned to you at the end of the matter.
If you want your file or any papers from it earlier, please ask your case worker.

blocks.title: Bank details and fraud warning
blocks.body:
Please be careful about emails or calls asking you to pay money or change bank details.
- We will never email you to say our bank details have changed.
- Phone us on a number you already know before you send any money.
- If you receive a suspicious message, tell us straight away.

blocks.title: How to contact us
blocks.body:
If you need to contact {{firm name}}, please write to {{firm address}} or use {{firm contact}} and quote reference {{our ref}}.
Your case worker is {{case worker}}. If they are not available, please ask for another member of the family team.

items.title: Acknowledgement of instructions
items.body:
Thank you for instructing {{firm name}}. This letter confirms that I have opened a file for you with our reference {{our ref}}.

I will send you our client care letter and terms of business separately. Please do not hesitate to contact me on {{firm contact}} if you have any questions.

Please send us your complete file, together with any original documents, and your final bill if one is outstanding. Please do not take any further steps without hearing from us.

items.title: Advice on a non-molestation order
items.body:
## What a non-molestation order does

A non-molestation order is a civil court order that tells {{other party}} not to use or threaten violence against you, and not to intimidate, harass or pester you or relevant children. Breaching it is a criminal offence.

## What happens next

We will prepare your application and statement. If there is a risk of harm, the court can make an order without notice to {{other party}}, and a hearing will follow at which they can respond.

If you are in danger, call 999. The National Domestic Abuse Helpline is on 0808 2000 247.

items.title: Advice on an occupation order
items.body:
## What an occupation order does

An occupation order decides who may live in or enter the home, or part of it, and can require {{other party}} to leave. The court weighs your housing needs, finances, the children and the effect on everyone of making or refusing the order.

## What we need from you

Please tell me who owns or rents the home, whose names are on the tenancy or mortgage, and who lives there now.

items.title: Advice on child arrangements, prohibited steps and specific issue orders
items.body:
## The orders you may ask for

- A child arrangements order decides where a child lives and the time they spend with each parent.
- A prohibited steps order stops a parent taking a step, such as removing a child from the country.
- A specific issue order decides a particular question, such as a school.

## Before the application

Unless an exemption applies, you will usually need to attend a MIAM first. If domestic abuse is involved, tell me so that I can explain the exemption.

The court's main concern is the welfare of the child.

items.title: Preparing for your hearing
items.body:
Your hearing is on {{next hearing date}} at {{hearing time}}, at {{court}}, case number {{case number}}.

- Please arrive at least 45 minutes early.
- Bring photo ID and any documents I have asked for.
- Tell me now if you need a separate waiting area or other safety arrangements.

I will meet you before the hearing to go through what to expect.

items.title: Advice on breach of an order
items.body:
You have told me that {{other party}} may have breached the order. Please keep a dated record of each incident, with messages, photographs and names of any witnesses.

If you are in immediate danger, call 999. A breach of a non-molestation order is a criminal offence and can also be dealt with by the family court, so tell me which you wish to pursue and I will advise on your options.

items.body:
IN THE {{court}}

CASE NO: {{case number}}

IN THE MATTER OF THE FAMILY LAW ACT 1996

BETWEEN

{{client name}} (Applicant)

-and-

{{other party}} (Respondent)

## FIRST STATEMENT OF THE APPLICANT

I, {{client name}}, of {{client address}}, will say as follows:

## Introduction

I make this statement in support of my application for an order transferring the tenancy of {{property address}} from the joint names of myself and the Respondent into my sole name.

The Respondent and I are associated persons within the meaning of Section 62 of the Family Law Act 1996 because the Respondent is my {{relationship}}. (Amend to state the basis: we were married; we were civil partners; we cohabited; we were in an intimate relationship of significant duration; we are the parents of a child.)

The tenancy of the property remains held jointly by myself and the Respondent.

## Background Information

I currently reside at the property known as: {{property address}}

The property is: {{tenancy type}} (A council tenancy; a housing association tenancy; a private tenancy. Delete as applicable.)

The tenancy is currently held in the names of: {{tenancy holders}}

The property consists of: {{number of bedrooms and property type}}

The Respondent previously resided at the property but no longer lives there.

The relationship between myself and the Respondent has permanently ended. There is no prospect of reconciliation.

## Children

The following children reside with me at the property:

- {{children}}

I am responsible for the day-to-day care of the children.

The children regard the property as their home.

The property is close to school, medical services, family members and support networks. Remaining in the property provides stability and continuity for the children.

## Previous Family Court Proceedings

(Delete this section if not applicable.)

Previous proceedings have taken place between myself and the Respondent.

On {{date of previous application}}, I applied for a Non-Molestation Order and/or an Occupation Order. (Delete as appropriate.)

In support of that application, I filed a witness statement detailing the history of abuse and relevant incidents. A copy of my previous witness statement is attached and marked "{{exhibit reference}}".

On {{date of previous order}}, the Court granted: {{details of the order}}

A copy of the Order is attached and marked "{{exhibit reference of the order}}".

The Respondent has not resided at the property since: {{date the respondent left the property}}

## Current Circumstances

I continue to reside at the property.

The Respondent resides at: {{respondent address}}

I am responsible for:

- Rent payments;
- Utility bills;
- Household expenses;
- Childcare arrangements.

The Respondent no longer contributes towards the day-to-day running of the household.

## Attempts to Resolve Matters

Before issuing this application, I attempted to resolve matters without Court intervention.

On {{date of letter to the respondent}}, I wrote to the Respondent requesting consent to transfer the tenancy into my sole name.

The Respondent was informed that:

- The tenancy could be transferred by agreement;
- He would be released from future tenancy obligations;
- Court proceedings would be issued if no response was received.

A copy of this correspondence is attached and marked "{{exhibit reference of the letter}}".

The Respondent failed to respond, refused consent, or failed to engage constructively. (Delete as applicable.)

It has therefore become necessary to ask the Court to determine the issue.

## Ongoing Difficulties

Despite the end of the relationship, difficulties continue because the tenancy remains in joint names.

The Respondent has continued to: {{details of issues arising from the joint tenancy}}

(For example: attempting to access the property; asserting rights over the property; interfering with housing arrangements; refusing to cooperate regarding tenancy matters.)

These matters have caused me stress, anxiety and uncertainty.

## Why the Tenancy Should Be Transferred

The Respondent has not resided at the property for a substantial period.

I am the person who occupies and maintains the property.

The children live at the property and regard it as their permanent home.

I have no suitable alternative accommodation available.

Requiring me and the children to move would:

- Disrupt education;
- Disrupt healthcare arrangements;
- Remove support networks;
- Cause emotional distress.

The Respondent does not require the property to meet his housing needs. The Respondent has: {{alternative accommodation details}}

I respectfully submit that it is fair and reasonable for the tenancy to be transferred into my sole name.

Such an order would:

- Reflect the reality of the parties' circumstances;
- Provide security of tenure;
- Promote stability for the children;
- Reduce future conflict between the parties.

I therefore respectfully request that the Court transfer the tenancy of {{property address}} into my sole name.

I further ask the Court to remove the Respondent from the tenancy agreement and make any additional directions necessary to give effect to the transfer.

## Relevant Considerations Under Schedule 7 Family Law Act 1996

I respectfully ask the Court to take into account the matters set out in Schedule 7 of the Family Law Act 1996. In particular:

## Housing Needs

My housing needs and those of the children require us to remain in the property.

The Respondent has alternative housing available to him.

## Financial Resources

My income is approximately: {{client income}} per month.

My primary outgoings include rent, utilities, food, childcare and transport.

The Respondent's approximate income is: {{respondent income}} per month.

The Respondent is better placed financially to secure alternative accommodation.

## Wellbeing

Remaining in the property promotes the physical and emotional wellbeing of myself and the children.

Relocating would cause significant disruption and hardship.

## Conduct

The Court may also consider the history of the parties' relationship and any previous findings or protective orders that have been made.

## Statement of Truth

I believe that the facts stated in this witness statement are true.

I understand that proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against anyone who makes, or causes to be made, a false statement in a document verified by a statement of truth without an honest belief in its truth.

Signed: ______________________________

Name: {{client name}}

Dated: ______________________________

## Typical exhibits

- TT1: Previous witness statement in support of NMO/OO application
- TT2: Occupation Order / Non-Molestation Order
- TT3: Letter requesting consent to transfer tenancy
- TT4: Tenancy Agreement
- TT5: Rent Statement
- TT6: Housing Association / Council correspondence
- TT7: Evidence of children's schooling and residence
- TT8: Proof of benefits and income

You and Mr Example separated in September 2026 after 12 years of marriage. You have two children, aged 9 and 6, who live with you.
